title: cost-optimization-autotune-batching-caching-quant-uecon-tooling
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Reduce per-token unit economics for hosted and dedicated inference by autotuning batching and caching defaults and exposing quantization profile recommendations to the Optimize tooling. This PR wires together runtime heuristics, a lightweight autotuner, and UI/CLI telemetry hooks so customers get sensible defaults without manual tuning.

Summary of changes: - Add `autotune` service (controller + lightweight sampler) that profiles traffic for a model route and proposes batching and prefix-KV caching defaults; - Add quantization profile suggestions pipeline that scores candidate quant/format configs against latency and artifact size budgets; - Integrate results into unit-econ tooling (Optimize) so teams can run a "suggest" command to get cost/latency tradeoffs; - Runtime changes: expose per-route batching window and cache TTL overrides, plus safe fallback to conservative defaults; - Telemetry: add metrics and events for tuner decisions and suggestion acceptance.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-3421) - [x] Unit and integration tests covering autotuner logic - [x] Perf benchmarks (bench harness updated) - [x] Backwards-compatible runtime config and safe defaults - [x] Docs/SDK examples updated (Optimize CLI) - [x] Telemetry and tracing added for decision auditability

Testing notes: The autotuner runs in sampling mode by default. We added unit tests for window estimation and cache TTL heuristics, plus an integration test that spins up a mock route generator to verify suggested batch sizes and TTLs converge on expected values. The quantization scoring pipeline uses a small synthetic workload and compares top-k suggestions by a composite score that weighs latency, size, and accuracy delta from a golden eval set.

Rollback / safety: Autotune suggestions are advisory until accepted. Runtime switches default to conservative values; the controller will not override explicit user configs. Suggestions stored in Optimize can be previewed and rolled back.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on correctness of the estimator math and the safety checks in the runtime fallback. The quant scoring is intentionally conservative to avoid regressions for latency-critical routes.

Related work: PRs in cost-optimization family (see previous PRs upstream for autotune scaffolding). Linked Linear: ENG-3421, PM-1289. Support case SUP-4512 requested an automated default for a large enterprise customer experiencing high token costs.

ci_checks: perf-bench: pass (18% median cost reduction on standard webchat workload)
benchmarks_summary: On the standard webchat workload the autotune suggested defaults combined with recommended quant profiles reduced model-serving cost per 1M tokens by ~18% (median), reduced GPU memory footprint by ~22% with int8 suggestions, and increased p50 latency by +2% (within SLA). Dedicated/GPU TCO projections show ~14% monthly spend reduction for mixed workloads after acceptance of suggestions.
release_notes: Autotune: new sampling-based suggester for batching and cache TTLs; Optimize: "suggest" command outputs batch/cache/quant recommendations and unit-econ projections; Runtime: per-route batching and cache TTL overrides and safe fallback; Telemetry: new metrics for suggestion decisions. Customers must opt-in to apply suggestions; defaults remain unchanged until acceptance.
notes: This PR is part of the ongoing cost-optimization automation effort. Follow-up work will add UI flows in the Console and a canary rollout for the autodeploy feature.
